T10.description: Task: write a Python function solve(n, edges) that returns the number of connected components of an undirected graph. The nodes are the integers 0 to n - 1, with 1 <= n <= 300. The argument edges is a list of pairs [u, v] with 0 <= u, v < n and u != v, each joining nodes u and v; 0 <= len(edges) <= 1500 and no pair of nodes is joined twice. A node with no edges forms a component on its own.

catalogue.mechanism: start a breadth-first traversal with a FIFO queue from every unvisited node and count the starts
start a depth-first traversal (recursion or an explicit LIFO stack) from every unvisited node and count the starts
union the endpoints of every edge in a disjoint-set forest and count the roots
give every node its own label and repeatedly sweep the edges, lowering labels to the neighbour minimum until nothing changes

T03.description: Task: write a Python function solve(nums, k) that returns the k-th smallest value in nums. The argument nums is a list of integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and every value lies between -10000 and 10000 inclusive; values may repeat. The argument k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(nums), counted from 1, so k = 1 asks for the minimum and k = len(nums) for the maximum. Repeated values are counted separately: for nums = [3, 1, 3] and k = 3 the answer is 3.

catalogue.mechanism: sort the whole list (sorted/list.sort or a hand-written full sort) and index position k-1
keep a heap bounded by k elements while scanning (or heapq.nsmallest/nlargest) and read its top
heapify all n values into one heap, then pop k times
partition around a pivot and recurse or loop into only the side that contains rank k
quickselect whose pivot is the median of the medians of groups of five, giving a worst-case linear selection
count occurrences of every value over the value range and walk the counts until k are covered
